title: How to correct HORBM, and what a correction does today
summary: Nine phrases are a correction. The reply is the honest miss "I don't know.", and the turn does not argue. A taught clause comes out only through retract_clause, which the turn does not call.
body:
On galion-one-voice commit 021e4d17 a correction is a closed table. Matching ignores case, and each row has to sit on a word boundary. The nine rows, quoted from the table, are "that's wrong", "thats wrong", "that is wrong", "actually it's", "actually its", "actually it is", "actually, it's", "actually, its", and "actually, it is". The comma inside a spoken "no, that's wrong" is not part of the match. "that's wrong" is the row. "that's wrongful" does not match, and neither does "actually it isn't", because the row has to end on a word boundary.

This read wins over a forget phrase and over a recall cue on the same line.

The policy answers with the honest miss "I don't know." The move is ask. It does not argue, and it does not repeat the previous sourced clause. The offline counter does not count the turn, and learn consent is left where the previous turn put it.

Saying one of those rows does not, inside the turn, replace a pin, and the turn does not call the learn pass. A taught clause can be taken back by retract_clause. The key is the trimmed speaker together with the trimmed text. The row id is not the key, because a rewrite allocates a fresh id for every copied row. Learn defaults to deny. The only grant is the trimmed word "grant". Without that grant the call is denied and the pack is not rewritten. When a live row has that speaker and that text, the other rows are copied in their live order and that one clause is removed. When none matches, the result is false and the pack is left untouched. Removing the last clause leaves an empty live pack, and the file stays. That call is not a withdrawal. The turn does not invoke it.

A line "forget that" also leaves a "learned:" snap in place. Taking the taught clause back is retract_clause, not the forget phrase.
